items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Benny was also in another level, one of jazz history‟s greats. He didn‟t mess around with us too much.

ctx.x: Yes, that‟s true, in the ‟40s, because I know . . .

Yeah, he made a couple of records that did pretty well. One of them was called Malibu, I think. Benny was also in another level, one of jazz history‟s greats. He didn‟t mess around with us too much. He did a little bit of t.v. writing during the ‟50s, but I don‟t think he was doing any jazz work. I don‟t know what – he must have been playing somewhere, but I don‟t know where. Maybe he traveled.

Probably so. I‟m looking at another record date here, Plays „Pal Joey.‟The reason why I bring up this date, this is a chamber jazz sextet. It included french horn and bassoon. You did arranging for this. Let me see if you have any recollections about that date. French horn and bassoon are not something that you normally see. These guys are doubling, obviously. Do you remember that? The Pal Joey, obviously this is a soundtrack.
